analysis.title: CPI Preview: Hot Headline, Tame Core, And An October Hike Nobody Wants
key_insights: September CPI (Wed Oct 14, 8:30am ET) sets the tone for the Oct 28 and December FOMC meetings. Consensus: headline +0.6% M/M (prev 0.4%), 3.6% Y/Y (prev 3.4%), driven by gasoline. Core +0.2% M/M (prev 0.3%), 2.5% Y/Y (prev 2.4%).
Market-implied odds of a 25bp October hike fell to about 20% from about 70% before the September payrolls report (29K, wage growth 3.0%, weakest since May 2021). December is still about 72% priced.

Fed officials turned patient after the jobs report. Jefferson and Williams say there is time to assess data, Waller wants more hikes but not at consecutive meetings, Bowman sees no urgency. Williams said one more hike this year is likely appropriate and nothing further in 2027.

FOMC minutes: all 19 officials backed the September hike and most see another by year-end as appropriate. Several participants cited AI buildout effects on core goods inflation, energy and labor costs, and aggregate demand.
Goldman expects core CPI +0.24% M/M (2.46% Y/Y) vs consensus mean 0.22%, and headline +0.59% (3.70% Y/Y, a tenth above consensus), with energy +5.0% and food +0.2%.
Goldman's component calls: used cars +0.5%, new cars +0.2%, auto insurance +0.2%, OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%, airfares +3.0%. Shelter (OER is about a third of core) is what keeps core in check.
Goldman forecasts September core PCE (due Oct 29) at +0.20%, lower than core CPI because cars weigh less in PCE and PCE airfare and health care source data should be more moderate.

Goldman expects core CPI about 0.2% in October (seasonal distortions from the data BLS did not collect during last year's government shutdown), then about 0.1% in November and December. This makes Goldman's economists more dovish than consensus for 2027. Risks tilt up if the oil disruption persists.

Jet fuel spot prices have roughly doubled since the start of the Iran war. Brent is above $105. The Russia/Ukraine energy ceasefire is described by Goldman's Rich Privorotsky as unable to survive a news cycle.
UMich one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%, with 5-10 year expectations at 3.5%.
UBS notes the Fed has never hiked in October ahead of US elections, and the Oct 28 meeting is one week before the midterms.
BofA's Michael Hartnett argued 'The Most Bullish Thing The Fed Can Do Now Is Hike'.

Options pricing: the SPX straddle for CPI day is 52bps ($41), one of the lowest this year vs a 78bp average of recent events. NDX is about 85bps vs a 111bp average. Goldman's desk saw a sizable buyer of SPX late-October downside (4.1mm vega in 10-delta puts), with skew steepening.

FX is priced richer: EURUSD CPI event gap is about 32bps (77th percentile of the 1-year distribution), major pairs at 20-32bps implied, all above the historical upper quartile. USDJPY implied vol is more than 4x its historical median.

Goldman desk view: downside asymmetry, with a soft print doing more damage to the hawks than a firm one does to the doves. A 10bp downside surprise on core would be meaningful for rates, while the MBS desk (Mark Flood) warns a marginal beat could be problematic for rates.

GS Swaps desk (Ilir Xholi) recommends receiving 10y10y swap at 5.26% (target 4.99%, stop 5.40%), arguing long-end term premium ran ahead of fundamentals. 10y10y rose 47bp between Sep 22 and Oct 7 while the 2Y swap did not move.

Author view: energy is now the inflation story, so a 0.2% core print buys the Fed a quiet October and not much more, while SPX straddles at their cheapest of the year price in only the benign outcome.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus and Goldman see a tame core held down by shelter (OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%). A benign print cements the patient camp, and Goldman's 0.1% core in November and December could mean no further hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy is feeding into airfares, autos and core goods, the FOMC flags AI-driven core goods inflation, and household expectations are at 4.7%. A hot, broad core print would revive October talk, and a 0.2% print buys only a quiet October.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot, broad-based core print on Wednesday would revive talk of an October move. A benign core print would cement waiting until December.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's desk sees a 10bp downside surprise on core as meaningful for rates, with real money buying the front end and street light on risk.
tension_points.bear_case: The MBS desk warns that given Goldman's 0.24% call, a marginal beat could prove problematic for rates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core CPI printing 10bp below consensus (downside) or a marginal beat above Goldman's 0.24% call.
